Assessment

A written examination for candidates to the eldership of Sun City Church

Candidate Name
Date Issued
Date Due

Instructions to the Candidate

  • This assessment has eight parts. Answer every question. If a question does not apply to you, write N/A.
  • There is no time limit. Take the time to answer thoughtfully and in your own words — depth matters more than length.
  • Part III (Bible & Doctrine) is not pass/fail. Even among our elders there are healthy shades of divergence. We are looking for how you think, not merely what you conclude. If your view on a matter is not fully formed, say so and explain your leanings.
  • Type your answers directly into this page. Your progress saves automatically in this browser — you can close it and come back anytime on the same device.
  • When finished, complete the affirmation on the final page, then click Finish & Download PDF in the bar at the bottom and email the PDF back to the church office.
  • Your answers will be reviewed by the Lead Pastor and current elders and will form the basis of your candidacy interview.

PART II — Personal

QUESTION 01

Briefly describe your personal spiritual journey (salvation, water baptism, Holy Spirit baptism, etc.).

QUESTION 02

What are your motivations for ministry and for becoming an Elder?

QUESTION 03

Read the qualifications of 1 Timothy 3:1–7, Titus 1:5–9, Acts 20:28–35 and 1 Peter 5:1–4. Summarize how you feel your life compares to these qualifications.

QUESTION 04

We believe stewardship should be modeled by those in leadership. What is your view on tithes and offerings, and do you tithe consistently? Do you give regularly beyond the tithe to other important church opportunities?

QUESTION 05

What major successes have you experienced, and how do these benefit you as a ministry leader?

QUESTION 06

What setbacks or failures have you experienced, and how will these work for your good as an Elder?

QUESTION 07

Describe any past involvement in other churches, including their affiliation with denominations or movements, your level of involvement, and your reason for leaving. Are you in good standing with previous pastors and leaders? Are there any unresolved issues?

QUESTION 08

Do you have any criminal record or child molestation charges? If so, explain.

QUESTION 09

Have you submitted a background check with Sun City Church? If not, would you be willing to fill one out immediately?

QUESTION 10

Can you make a commitment of a minimum of 3–5 years as an Elder?

PART III — Bible & Doctrine

Please do not view this section as pass/fail. Even among the elders, where there is general agreement on these subjects, there would still be shades of divergence — and that is healthy. These questions help us get to know a candidate’s perspective. Some questions ask about concepts articulated in our Statement of Faith; we are not only looking for whether you agree, but how you would explain it in your own words. If you need more detail before you can answer, say so or reach out for clarification. It’s alright if your opinions are not fully formed on a matter; simply state this and explain your leanings.

QUESTION 11

Do you fully agree with all of the official doctrinal statements of Sun City Church as defined in our Statement of Faith? If there are any points of uncertainty, please mention them and explain your beliefs or assumptions on those points.

QUESTION 12

What is your view of Scripture? What is it? What is its origin? How do we relate to it? Please speak to the subject of authority, infallibility, and its place in forming church policy.

QUESTION 13

In your opinion, what are some of the most important principles for interpreting Scripture accurately?

QUESTION 14

How would you articulate the gospel to an unbeliever? What are the primary components of the gospel?

QUESTION 15

While the church may have many roles and ministries, what would you say is its primary purpose according to Scripture? How should that purpose affect things like service planning, administration, staffing, and the church’s relationship to society?

QUESTION 16

What is your view on church discipline (i.e., addressing sin in a church member)? Should it ever lead to a member being removed from church fellowship? If so, under what circumstances? What Scripture premise validates your stance?

QUESTION 17

What is your current view on racism? What role should the church play (if any) in addressing this issue?

QUESTION 18

Is a homosexual relationship sinful if it is loving, consensual, and monogamous (in legal marriage)? Explain.

QUESTION 19

Do you think Christians can always find complete freedom from same-sex attraction (SSA) if they struggle with it? If yes, explain. If no, how would you advise them in their journey of sanctification in this area?

QUESTION 20

Do you think Christians are free to discover or decide their own gender identity regardless of their biological sex?

QUESTION 21

How would you explain Scripture’s teaching on hell as you understand it? Speak to the following: What is it? Who goes there? For how long? Who sends them?

QUESTION 22

For each doctrine or practice below, mark the level of importance you would assign it:

  • Die for it — all Christians must agree on this
  • Divide over it — we must agree in order to go to church together, especially in leadership
  • Discuss it — we can agree to disagree and continue debate and discussion in fellowship
Doctrine / PracticeDie for itDivide over itDiscuss it
The deity of Jesus
The bodily resurrection of Jesus
The infallibility of Scripture
Water baptism
Tithing
Sign gifts (speaking in tongues, prophecy, etc.)
Women in ministry leadership
The model of church government
The place of Israel in God's program
Social consumption of alcohol (not drunkenness)

Views on Debated Doctrines

There are some doctrines on which Christians tend to have a greater diversity of views. Usually they “agree to disagree” on these matters, but a general awareness of your leanings is helpful. Select the option that best represents your view.
